content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler Bananas, Stage 2 are soft, ripe bananas prepared especially for children aged 6 to 12 months. They are rich in natural sugars, vitamins and minerals, easy to digest and ideal for first foods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bananas are one of the first fruits typically introduced into an infant's diet.
High potassium content helps maintain fluid and electrolyte balance in babies.
Bananas are naturally gluten‑free and contain no lactose.
A ripe banana can be turned into a smooth puree without added sugar or salt.
The natural sweetness of bananas can help develop a positive taste for fruits.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports nervous system development and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids normal heart and muscle function and helps regulate water balance.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in bananas helps normalize stool and prevent constipation.

items.title: Low allergen potential
items.content: Bananas rarely cause allergic reactions, making them a safe choice for most infants.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole banana pieces can pose a choking risk for children under 12 months – offer as puree or very finely mashed.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Although uncommon, some infants may develop a banana allergy; stop feeding if rash or swelling appears.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Bananas contain natural sugars; for children at risk of tooth decay, serve without added sweeteners and clean teeth after meals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve banana as a smooth puree, mash with a fork, or blend with other fruit or vegetable purees. For babies older than 9 months, small soft pieces can be offered once you are sure they do not pose a choking risk.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ripe bananas at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, place them in the refrigerator—they stay fresh for up to 5 days. Cut or pureed banana should be stored in an airtight container in the fridge and used within 24 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: The NFS Fish Sandwich is a ready‑to‑eat sandwich featuring a breaded fish fillet, fresh vegetables and a creamy sauce between a soft bun. It is designed for a quick snack at home or at the office.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sandwich is part of the NFS line, focused on convenient and nutritious ready meals.
The breading uses fish sourced from environmentally clean waters, ensuring low heavy‑metal levels.
Vegetables are grown without synthetic pesticides.
Each sandwich is sealed in an individual vacuum package that keeps it fresh for up to 12 months.
The product has been tested for easy microwave reheating.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: The fish provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: One sandwich delivers about 20 g of protein, essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and niacin, important for nervous system function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The sandwich contains mainly polyunsaturated fats, making it heart‑friendly.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Fresh veggies add dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People with known seafood allergies may experience allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sandwich contains a moderate amount of salt; individuals limiting sodium should consider portion size.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.content: When microwaving, follow the recommended time to avoid drying out the fish.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: After opening, consume within 24 hours and keep refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the sandwich in the microwave for 1–2 minutes (or as instructed), let it cool slightly, and enjoy. Optionally add fresh lettuce or a lemon wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened sandwich in a cool, dry place at 0 °C to +25 °C. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within a day.

content.title: About
content.content: Rice, white, cooked is a boiled grain product made from polished white rice (Oryza sativa). It has a soft texture, neutral flavor, and is widely used as a side dish, base for meals, and ingredient in cuisines worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice is a staple food for more than half of the world’s population.
White rice loses most of its fiber and nutrients during milling, but remains a good source of energy.
In Japan, rice is often served plain to highlight its natural taste.
In some cultures rice is used in traditional desserts such as rice pudding.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: White rice is rich in carbohydrates that quickly convert to glucose, providing a rapid energy boost.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Cooked rice is soft and gentle on the stomach, making it suitable for people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: A 100‑g serving of cooked rice contains less than 1 g of fat, fitting low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice provides thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, phosphorus, and small amounts of iron.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Compared with whole‑grain varieties, white rice provides little dietary fiber, which can affect digestion.

items.title: Arsenic
items.content: In some regions rice can accumulate arsenic from the soil; choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rice can be served as a side to meat, fish or vegetables, used in sushi, pilaf, soups and salads. It can also be turned into rice porridge or added to baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to steaming temperature before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: A tomato sandwich on white bread consists of fresh slices of ripe tomatoes, lettuce leaves, and a light spread of mayonnaise or mustard, placed between two pieces of soft white bread. This light dish is popular in cafés and home meals, offering a bright flavor and refreshing texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their characteristic red color.
White bread is often used in sandwiches because its neutral taste does not overpower the flavor of tomatoes.
Tomato sandwiches are commonly served in the summer when tomatoes are at their peak season.
In some regions, avocado slices are added for a creamier texture.
The classic American BLT (bacon, lettuce, tomato) is often simplified to a lighter version without bacon—just tomato and lettuce.

items.title: Rich in Vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains Lycopene
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties and may help protect against certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Low in Calories
items.content: A tomato sandwich on white bread typically has modest calorie content, making it a good choice for a light snack.

items.title: Source of Fiber
items.content: Tomatoes and lettuce supply dietary fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Tomatoes are about 95% water, helping to keep the body hydrated.

items.title: Tomato Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, manifesting as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Tomatoes can increase stomach acidity, which may be problematic for people with gastritis or heartburn.

items.title: Glutamate Content
items.content: Tomatoes naturally contain glutamate, which in large amounts can trigger headaches in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare the sandwich by layering tomato slices and lettuce between two pieces of white bread, spreading a thin layer of mayonnaise, mustard, or a light sauce. A pinch of salt and freshly ground black pepper can enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best enjoyed immediately. If you need to store it, wrap it tightly in plastic film and keep it in the refrigerator for no more than 4 hours to prevent the bread from drying out and the tomatoes from losing freshness.
